day-10-act-01.title: Paths, encodings, and safe file reads
day-10-act-01.prerequisites: Complete the previous activity; use the listed recovery link if blocked.
day-10-act-01.objective: Read a text file with an explicit UTF-8 encoding inside a with block and count its non-empty lines. Predict the count before running, then explain why a relative path depends on the current working directory.
day-10-act-01.assistance_policy_label: Assistance allowed only after prediction and observed evidence are recorded.
day-10-act-01.instructions:
Study source: within this activity's existing reading/practice time, use Automate the Boring Stuff with Python, 3rd edition, Chapter 10; Practice Questions; Appendix B answers, then explain one connection to the local task in your own words. Keep the local exercise and acceptance checks; use its original explanation if the external source is unavailable. In a fresh directory create notes.txt containing exactly three lines: alpha, beta, gamma. A relative path such as open("notes.txt") is resolved against Path.cwd(), not against the folder that holds the script. Iterating the file object yields one line at a time; each line keeps its "
" terminator except possibly the last one, which has none when the file does not end with a newline (a file written as "alpha
beta
gamma" yields 'gamma' as its final line). line.strip() removes that newline and any surrounding whitespace, so it decides whether a line is empty. The with block is predefined cleanup: it closes the file even if reading raises an exception.
day-10-act-01.exercise_prompt:
count = 0
with open("notes.txt", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    for line in f:
        if line.strip():
            count += 1
print(count, f.closed)
Before running, write down the exact line this prints and explain why each of the two values comes out the way it does. Would the result change if notes.txt did not end with a newline?
day-10-act-01.hint: Predict before running. If the path confuses you, print Path.cwd() first. Compare the number of iterations with the number of non-empty lines; strip() decides emptiness, not the raw line.
day-10-act-01.answer:
count = 0
with open("notes.txt", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    for line in f:
        if line.strip():
            count += 1
print(count, f.closed)
Output: 3 True. Trace: the loop receives 'alpha\n', 'beta\n', 'gamma\n' (or 'gamma' when the file has no final newline); each is non-empty after strip(), so count reaches 3, and a trailing newline on the last line does not create a fourth line. print runs after the with block has exited, so f is already closed and f.closed is True.
day-10-act-01.mastery_criterion: Your prediction matches the observed output, you state that relative paths resolve against Path.cwd(), and you show the file object's closed state (f.closed) after the with block exits.

day-10-act-02.title: Diagnose a missing file before editing code
day-10-act-02.prerequisites: Complete the previous activity; use the listed recovery link if blocked.
day-10-act-02.objective: Reproduce FileNotFoundError from open("data/notes.txt") and classify the cause as an absent file or a wrong working directory by gathering Path.exists() and Path.cwd() evidence before editing any code.
day-10-act-02.assistance_policy_label: Assistance allowed only after prediction and observed evidence are recorded.
day-10-act-02.instructions: Work only in a disposable fixture: the scripts in this activity build project/ (containing reader.py and data/notes.txt) and an empty sibling folder outside/ inside a fresh temporary directory that is deleted on exit, so the result never depends on what happens to exist in your home directory or real projects. The message [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'data/notes.txt' says only that the relative path did not resolve from the current working directory; it cannot separate the two causes. Gather evidence first: compare Path.cwd() with the script's folder, evaluate Path("data/notes.txt").exists() (relative to the cwd), and evaluate (BASE / "data" / "notes.txt").exists() with BASE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent (relative to the script). If the anchored path exists but the relative one does not, the working directory is wrong: open(BASE / "data" / "notes.txt", encoding="utf-8"). If the anchored path is also missing, the fixture is genuinely absent and must be created or restored; changing the code will not help.
day-10-act-02.exercise_prompt:
Run this script from any directory. It builds the disposable fixture, then runs the unmodified reader.py (which opens the relative path data/notes.txt) once with the project folder as the cwd and once with outside/ as the cwd. Before running, predict the exit code and every printed line of both runs. Then classify the cause from the evidence and write the minimal fix for reader.py without rewriting its counting logic.

```python
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

READER = (
    "from pathlib import Path\n"
    "print('cwd is project:', Path.cwd() == Path(__file__).resolve().parent)\n"
    "print('exists:', Path('data/notes.txt').exists())\n"
    "with open('data/notes.txt', encoding='utf-8') as f:\n"
    "    print('lines:', sum(1 for line in f if line.strip()))\n"
)

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    root = Path(tmp).resolve()
    project = root / "project"
    outside = root / "outside"
    (project / "data").mkdir(parents=True)
    outside.mkdir()
    (project / "data" / "notes.txt").write_text("alpha\nbeta\ngamma\n", encoding="utf-8")
    (project / "reader.py").write_text(READER, encoding="utf-8")
    for label, cwd in [("project", project), ("outside", outside)]:
        run = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(project / "reader.py")],
                             cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True)
        print(f"[{label}] exit={run.returncode}")
        print(run.stdout, end="")
        if run.stderr:
            print(run.stderr.strip().splitlines()[-1])
```
day-10-act-02.hint: Never fix a missing-file error by regenerating code. Gather cwd and exists() evidence first, then decide whether the fix belongs to the path anchor or to the fixture.
day-10-act-02.answer:
Observed output of the exercise script (the same on every machine, because the fixture is private):

```text
[project] exit=0
cwd is project: True
exists: True
lines: 3
[outside] exit=1
cwd is project: False
exists: False
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'data/notes.txt'
```

Diagnosis: the file exists (exists: True when the cwd is the project), but the second run has a different cwd (cwd is project: False), so the relative path resolves to outside/data/notes.txt, which does not exist. The cause is the working directory, not an absent file. Minimal fix: anchor the path to the script with BASE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent and open BASE / "data" / "notes.txt"; the counting line stays unchanged. The complete reference below writes the anchored reader into a fresh fixture, runs it from both folders, then deletes the data file to show the other cause: when the anchored path itself does not exist, no code change helps, and restoring the fixture does.

```python
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

FIXED = (
    "from pathlib import Path\n"
    "BASE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent\n"
    "with open(BASE / 'data' / 'notes.txt', encoding='utf-8') as f:\n"
    "    print('lines:', sum(1 for line in f if line.strip()))\n"
)


def run(script, cwd):
    done = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(script)],
                          cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if done.returncode == 0:
        return f"exit=0 {done.stdout.strip()}"
    last = done.stderr.strip().splitlines()[-1]
    return f"exit={done.returncode} {last.split(':')[0]}"


with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    root = Path(tmp).resolve()
    project = root / "project"
    outside = root / "outside"
    notes = project / "data" / "notes.txt"
    notes.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    outside.mkdir()
    notes.write_text("alpha\nbeta\ngamma\n", encoding="utf-8")
    reader = project / "reader.py"
    reader.write_text(FIXED, encoding="utf-8")
    print("anchored, from outside:", run(reader, outside))
    print("anchored, from project:", run(reader, project))
    notes.unlink()
    print("fixture deleted, anchored path exists:", notes.exists())
    print("anchored, from project:", run(reader, project))
    notes.write_text("alpha\nbeta\ngamma\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print("fixture restored:", run(reader, outside))
```

Expected output:

```text
anchored, from outside: exit=0 lines: 3
anchored, from project: exit=0 lines: 3
fixture deleted, anchored path exists: False
anchored, from project: exit=1 FileNotFoundError
fixture restored: exit=0 lines: 3
```
day-10-act-02.mastery_criterion: Your log states which of the two causes applied, shows the cwd/exists() evidence that proves it, and applies the minimal fix (path anchor or fixture restore) instead of rewriting the reader.

day-10-act-03.title: Invalid content: tolerant parsing with a skip report
day-10-act-03.prerequisites: Complete the previous activity; use the listed recovery link if blocked.
day-10-act-03.objective: Parse a scores file in which one row is malformed: record each skipped line number and keep going. Distinguish UnicodeDecodeError (bytes decoded with the wrong encoding) from ValueError (valid text, invalid value).
day-10-act-03.assistance_policy_label: Assistance allowed only after prediction and observed evidence are recorded.
day-10-act-03.instructions: Rows look like ana,7. int("x9") raises ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'x9'. Wrap only the int(raw) call in try/except ValueError, append the line number to a skipped list, and store the score only when parsing succeeded. Decoding problems are a different failure: the bytes b'caf\xe9' (café saved as Latin-1) are not valid UTF-8, so b'caf\xe9'.decode("utf-8") raises UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xe9 in position 3: unexpected end of data. Do not generalize this to "every Latin-1 file fails as UTF-8": a pure-ASCII file decodes identically under both, and some byte sequences are valid in both encodings but mean different text (b'caf\xc3\xa9' is café in UTF-8 but cafÃ© in Latin-1), so a decode that succeeds does not prove the encoding is right. The fix is to name the real encoding — never errors="ignore", which silently drops undecodable bytes and hides the problem.
day-10-act-03.exercise_prompt:
Given rows ana,7 / bo,x9 / cy,5 (one per line), predict the result of a tolerant reader before running: which rows end up in scores, and which line numbers end up in skipped. Then run this complete program from any directory; it writes its own scores.txt fixture into a temporary directory that is deleted afterwards and defines scores and skipped before the loop. Keep the try block limited to int(raw), and store a score only after parsing succeeded.

```python
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    path = Path(tmp) / "scores.txt"
    path.write_text("ana,7\nbo,x9\ncy,5\n", encoding="utf-8")
    scores = {}
    skipped = []
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for lineno, line in enumerate(f, 1):
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            name, _, raw = line.rpartition(",")
            try:
                score = int(raw)
            except ValueError:
                skipped.append(lineno)
                continue
            scores[name] = score
    print(scores, skipped)
```
day-10-act-03.hint: Make the try block as small as possible — the int(raw) call only — so you never swallow errors from open() or the line split. Record line numbers, not just a count.
day-10-act-03.answer:
Prediction and observed output:

```text
{'ana': 7, 'cy': 5} [2]
```

Line 2 (bo,x9) raises ValueError inside the try, so its number goes into skipped and continue skips the assignment; lines 1 and 3 reach scores[name] = score. The try wraps only int(raw), so a failing open() or a bug in the split still surfaces as a traceback instead of being silently counted as a bad row. enumerate(f, 1) numbers physical lines, so a blank line still advances the count. A decoding problem is a different failure class; this program contrasts it with ValueError:

```python
data = "café".encode("latin-1")
print(data)
try:
    data.decode("utf-8")
except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
    print(type(exc).__name__ + ":", exc)
print(data.decode("latin-1") == "café")
print(b"plain ascii".decode("utf-8") == b"plain ascii".decode("latin-1"))
both = b"caf\xc3\xa9"
as_utf8 = both.decode("utf-8")
as_latin1 = both.decode("latin-1")
print(as_utf8 == "café", as_latin1 == "cafÃ©", len(as_utf8), len(as_latin1))
```

Expected output:

```text
b'caf\xe9'
UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xe9 in position 3: unexpected end of data
True
True
True True 4 5
```

b'caf\xe9' is café in Latin-1 and is not valid UTF-8, so decoding it as UTF-8 raises UnicodeDecodeError; the fix is to declare the real encoding (here encoding="latin-1"). Pure ASCII decodes the same under both encodings, and b'caf\xc3\xa9' decodes successfully under both but to different text (café, 4 characters, versus cafÃ©, 5 characters), so a decode that succeeds is not proof that the declared encoding is right. ValueError, by contrast, means the text decoded fine but one row's value is invalid.
day-10-act-03.mastery_criterion: Valid rows are processed, skipped line numbers are recorded, and you correctly name both failure types: UnicodeDecodeError means fix the declared encoding; ValueError means one row's content was invalid.

day-10-act-04.title: Independent file summary and recovery plan
day-10-act-04.prerequisites: Complete the previous activity; use the listed recovery link if blocked.
day-10-act-04.objective: Closed-book: write summarize_scores(path) returning {"scores": {name: best}, "skipped": [line numbers], "missing": bool}. It must handle a valid file, a file with a malformed row, and a missing file without crashing.
day-10-act-04.instructions: Predict all three fixture results before coding, and do not consult an answer or AI during the check. Recovery links if blocked: day-10-act-02 for a missing file, day-10-act-03 for a malformed row.
day-10-act-04.exercise_prompt: Expected contract (create the fixtures in a fresh temporary directory, for example with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(), so no other file can interfere): s1.txt containing ana,7 / bo,9 / ana,8 returns {'scores': {'ana': 8, 'bo': 9}, 'skipped': [], 'missing': False} because 8 beats 7 for ana. s2.txt containing ana,7 / bo,x9 / cy,5 returns {'scores': {'ana': 7, 'cy': 5}, 'skipped': [2], 'missing': False} because line 2 is malformed. A path inside that temporary directory that was never created, such as missing.txt, returns {'scores': {}, 'skipped': [], 'missing': True} instead of raising.
